title: C12 Server Action SECURITY (break then harden)

files_forbidden: all app/(challenges)/* directories not belonging to this task

acceptance_criteria: The hardened (secure) action rejects an unauthenticated mutation invoked by a raw POST that bypasses the UI, AND rejects a mutation by an authenticated user who does not own the target review; in both cases the backing store is NOT mutated (QA critical: the C12 Server Action reference solution rejects an unauthorized mutation).

The secure action performs auth via the FROZEN lib/auth getSession, then an authorization check (can THIS user edit THIS review?), then zod schema validation of inputs before any write — in that order.
NOTES.md explains Next.js' built-in Server Action origin/CSRF protection vs app-level checks, and documents a rate-limit concept; it makes clear that origin protection alone is NOT authorization.

solutions/c12-action-security/insecure/ ships a deliberately insecure action (no auth/authorization) with a README showing how to exploit it (forge request / reuse-or-tamper session); the insecure code lives only under solutions/ and is never imported by the live app (QA: reference solutions stored separately).

The c12 _meta folder contains spec.md (non-empty acceptance criteria), defend-it.md (3-5 from-memory questions with model answers), verification.md, and a discoverable challenge.config.ts; auth is consumed via the frozen interface only and lib/auth is not edited.
output_format: code plus plain English explanation of every non-obvious decision
